entries.title: Attach gated takeaways (slides, PDFs, links) to webinar pages with a single email gate
entries.summary: Organizers can now attach downloadable takeaways — slides, PDFs, worksheets, or links — to a webinar's agent page via the API, MCP (Ask), or a direct upload. Each takeaway can be marked **Gated**, which shows a single email-capture dialog per page view; one email submission unlocks all gated takeaways **and** any gated recording on the same page. Downloads are recorded as `content.downloaded` Signals on the person's CRM timeline and in engaged-people counts.

where.path: Marketing → Events → [Webinar] → Assets (via API/MCP or agent page)

entries.use_case: Webinar organizers who share slides, worksheets or resource PDFs after a session can now attach those files directly to the webinar's public page and gate them behind an email capture — turning every download into a qualified lead without building a separate landing page. Engagement is automatically tracked on each person's CRM timeline.

cs_action.note: The embeds client half (lennd/sessionboard-embeds feature/webinar-takeaways) requires a manual PROD publish after merge; confirm that step is complete before telling customers the feature is live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to share post-webinar resources, capture leads from on-demand content, or track who downloaded slides.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any Marketing customer running webinars who wants to gate downloadable resources and track engagement — especially teams that currently share slides via a separate email or landing page.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → [Webinar] → Assets (API/MCP); public page shows the Assets block
internal.gotchas: Gated videos no longer remember the grant in localStorage — a page reload will show the email gate again. The embeds PROD publish is manual; the feature is not fully live until that step is done. File uploads are capped at 100 MB (presigned PUT) or 10 MB (base64); no Filestack.
internal.talk_track: After your webinar, attach the slides and any worksheets right from Claude or ChatGPT using Ask. Gate them with one toggle — visitors enter their email once and instantly get access to every takeaway and the recording. Every download shows up on their CRM timeline so you know exactly who’s engaged.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining how to attach takeaways (via API, MCP/Ask, or upload), how to toggle the gated flag, what the email-gate dialog looks like for visitors, and how download Signals appear on a person's CRM timeline.
draft.why_use_it: Webinar pages in Sessionboard Marketing can host the recording, speaker bios, and now downloadable takeaways — all in one place. Gating takeaways behind an email form lets you capture intent from people who missed the live session or want to revisit the material, and every download is logged as a Signal so your team can see exactly who engaged and follow up. Because one email entry unlocks every gated asset and the recording on the page, visitors get a smooth experience while you get a complete picture of their interest.

entries.title: CRM sidebar nests contact types under All Contacts
entries.summary: In the new navigation, **Speakers**, **Chairpersons**, **Moderators**, **Submitters**, **Additional Contacts** and any custom session roles now appear indented under **All Contacts** in the **CRM → People** section, making it clear they are subsets of the full contact list. **Attendees** remains at the top level because it reflects registration data rather than a contact type. A contact type pinned to the Pinned zone is not indented.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → New Navigation

entries.use_case: Organizers who work across multiple contact types can now see at a glance that Speakers, Chairpersons, Moderators and other role views are filtered subsets of All Contacts, reducing confusion about where to look for a person.

cs_action.note: Automatic for customers already on the New Navigation preview; no configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer on the New Navigation preview asks why contact type views look different, or when demoing the new navigation to prospects.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the New Navigation limited release who works with multiple contact types (speakers, chairpersons, moderators, etc.).
internal.gotchas: Nesting is positional within the CRM section only — a contact type pinned to the Pinned zone will not be indented. The legacy sidebar is unchanged.
internal.talk_track: In the new navigation, the CRM sidebar now shows Speakers, Chairpersons, Moderators and other role views indented under All Contacts, so it's immediately obvious they're filtered subsets rather than separate lists.

draft.docs_gap: The sidebar guide should add a note explaining that in the new navigation, CRM contact-type views (Speakers, Chairpersons, Moderators, Submitters, Additional Contacts, custom roles) are displayed indented under All Contacts, and that Attendees remains at the top level.
draft.why_use_it: The sidebar is your primary way to move between modules and filtered views in Sessionboard. Visual hierarchy in the CRM People section helps you understand the relationship between contact types and the full contact list, so you reach the right view faster and avoid hunting through flat lists of seemingly equal items.

entries.title: Org portal forms, auth pages and hero text are safer and more accessible
entries.summary: Three security and accessibility gaps in the org portal are resolved. Custom HTML in application, session and speaker form content blocks, section descriptions, the **Reviewer Instructions** banner, the welcome-form privacy note and the submitter home description is now sanitized before rendering, so injected scripts no longer execute. Faded branding text on the landing hero, login, verify, welcome and logout cards is replaced with full-opacity colour, meeting the 4.5:1 contrast minimum. The **Verify** page (`/auth/verify`) now has a `main` landmark, an `h1` heading and a working **Skip to main content** link in every state.

where.path: Portal → submission forms, auth pages and landing hero

entries.use_case: Organisations that embed custom HTML in portal form content blocks or section descriptions can be confident that malicious script payloads will not execute for submitters or reviewers. Participants using screen readers or keyboard navigation on the magic-link verify page can now move through the page correctly.

cs_action.note: All three fixes are automatic and require no configuration. The XSS sanitization preserves safe formatting such as bold and links while stripping executable payloads.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports unexpected script execution in portal forms, or when a customer's accessibility team flags contrast or landmark issues on the org portal auth pages.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using the org portal, especially those who allow organizers to enter custom HTML in form content blocks or section descriptions.
internal.staff_path: Portal → any application, session or speaker form with a content block or section description; /auth/verify magic-link page
internal.gotchas: The admin custom footer HTML field is intentionally excluded from sanitization because it sits alongside a custom JS field; only form content blocks and section descriptions are sanitized.
internal.talk_track: Script payloads in portal form content blocks are now stripped automatically, bold and link formatting is preserved, the verify page is keyboard-navigable, and faded text on auth cards now meets WCAG AA contrast.

draft.docs_gap: The accessibility guide should note that org portal auth pages (login, verify, welcome, logout) meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and landmark requirements, and that custom HTML in form content blocks is sanitized to prevent script injection.

entries.title: Agenda, session and room embeds use correct heading hierarchy; form embeds get an accessible iframe title
entries.summary: Child headings inside session, schedule, agenda, room, sponsor and filter-dialog embeds now derive from the embed's **Heading Level** setting instead of being hard-coded, so the published page's heading hierarchy is always correct for screen readers. The **`<sessionboard-form>`** embed also now reads the framed form's title and sets it as the iframe's accessible name automatically, with a manual **`title=`** attribute available as an override.

where.path: Sessions → Embeds → (any agenda, session, schedule, room or form embed)

entries.use_case: Organisations that must meet WCAG accessibility standards can now embed their agenda, session list, rooms and forms on external websites without introducing heading-level violations or unlabelled iframes — reducing remediation work before audits or procurement reviews.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic for all embeds already published; no reconfiguration needed. The heading hierarchy now respects the Heading Level setting end-to-end.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer mentions WCAG compliance, an accessibility audit, or a procurement requirement that includes assistive-technology testing of their event website.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer embedding agenda, session, room or form widgets on a public or intranet website, especially those in government, higher education, healthcare or enterprise sectors with formal accessibility obligations.
internal.gotchas: The form iframe title fix requires the companion portal change (lennd/sessionboard-web-org-portal on the same branch) to be deployed; without it the iframe title will not be set automatically.
internal.talk_track: If your web team has flagged heading-level or unlabelled-iframe issues in an accessibility scan of your event site, these are now resolved automatically — no changes to your embed code required.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that child headings inside all embed types (sessions, schedule, agenda, rooms, sponsors, filter dialog) inherit the Heading Level setting, and that the form embed automatically sets its iframe title from the framed form — with a note that a manual title= attribute overrides it.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard embeds let you drop a live, always-current agenda, session list, room grid or submission form directly onto any webpage without rebuilding it yourself. The **Heading Level** setting controls where the embed sits in your page's document outline, so assistive technologies and search engines read the hierarchy correctly. Form embeds carry an accessible name so screen readers announce what the iframe contains before a visitor enters it.

entries.title: Five accessibility fixes: keyboard multi-select, XSS sanitisation, mobile drawer focus trap, track chip contrast, and site 404 page
entries.summary: Five accessibility issues found in the Wave 7a audit are resolved. **Space** now toggles a highlighted option in multi-select fields when the search box is empty (and still types when it contains text). Admin-supplied HTML in field help text and label tooltips is sanitised before rendering, closing an XSS vector on task, application, session and speaker forms. The mobile navigation drawer now traps focus — **Tab** and **Shift+Tab** cycle only between the drawer and its toggle, **Escape** closes it and returns focus to the toggle. Track chips on gallery cards now use a calculated ink colour that meets contrast requirements against any track colour. Navigating to an unknown path inside a Site now shows a proper **Page not found** page with a heading, a link home, and a correctly titled browser tab; the sign-in tab is also titled **Sign in — \<Site name\>**.

where.path: Portal → any form or gallery page; Site → any page

entries.use_case: Organisations that need WCAG-conformant portals and sites — particularly those serving attendees who rely on keyboard navigation or assistive technology — will find that multi-select fields, mobile navigation, gallery track chips, and site error pages now behave correctly without any configuration change.

cs_action.note: All five fixes are automatic; no configuration is required. Behaviour changes are limited to keyboard interaction, HTML sanitisation, colour contrast, and the 404 page — nothing visible to organizers in the admin.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about WCAG compliance, accessibility audits, or reports a keyboard/screen-reader issue in portals or sites.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose attendees or speakers use assistive technology, or who must meet accessibility requirements for their organisation.
internal.staff_path: Portal → any form task; Site → unknown URL path; Site → content gallery card with a track chip
internal.gotchas: The XSS sanitisation fix affects all forms that use FieldLabelWithTooltip (task, application, session, speaker forms). Any admin-supplied HTML that relied on unsanitised attributes (e.g. onerror handlers) will now be stripped — this is intentional and correct.
internal.talk_track: Wave 7a of our accessibility programme closes five keyboard and contrast issues in portals and sites. Everything ships automatically — no action needed from the customer.

draft.docs_gap: The accessibility guide should note the specific WCAG criteria addressed by each fix (keyboard multi-select, focus trap, colour contrast, sanitised help text, 404 page) and reference the Wave audit programme so customers can point auditors to the conformance record.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's portals and sites are designed to be usable by every participant, including those who navigate by keyboard or use a screen reader. The platform is regularly audited against WCAG 2.1 AA, and fixes are shipped as soon as issues are confirmed. Organizers can share portal and site links with confidence that the experience meets accessibility standards for all attendees.

entries.title: Rich-text heading menu in the session edit sheet is now clickable with the mouse
entries.summary: In the portal's session edit sheet, the **Paragraph / Heading 2–4** dropdown in the rich-text toolbar can now be opened and selected with the mouse. Previously, Radix's modal overlay blocked pointer events on the editor's floating menu, so only keyboard arrow keys worked.

where.path: Portals → [portal] → session edit sheet → rich-text toolbar

entries.use_case: Speakers and organizers editing session descriptions in the portal can now click the **Paragraph / Heading 2–4** menu with the mouse instead of being forced to use arrow keys, making rich-text formatting work as expected.

cs_action.note: Automatic fix; no configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that the heading or paragraph style picker in the portal session edit sheet does not respond to mouse clicks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using rich-text session description fields in a speaker portal.
internal.staff_path: Portals → [portal] → open a session → rich-text toolbar → Paragraph / Heading dropdown
internal.gotchas: Fix applies to the HugeRTE toolbar menu (`.tox-hugerte-aux`); the same fix was previously applied to TinyMCE (`.tox-tinymce-aux`) for the Filestack picker.
internal.talk_track: The heading style picker in the session edit sheet now works with the mouse — speakers no longer need to use arrow keys to change text formatting.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the session edit sheet supports a rich-text toolbar with paragraph and heading styles selectable by mouse.

entries.title: Manage custom domain redirect rules for Marketing pages via the Public API and AI assistants
entries.summary: Three new endpoints let you read, write and delete URL redirect rules on a Marketing pages custom domain through the Public API and MCP server: `GET /v1/organization/:orgId/marketing/pages/domains/:domainId/redirects`, `PUT …/redirects` (supports full list replacement, incremental `ops`, or `restore_version` with optional optimistic-lock via `if_version`), and `DELETE …/redirects/:redirectId`. Pass `?history=true` on the GET to retrieve every saved version with author, timestamp and a diff of what changed.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable site_domains; then use the Public API at /v1/organization/:orgId/marketing/pages/domains/:domainId/redirects

entries.use_case: Teams that manage Marketing page custom domains programmatically — for example, migrating a large set of legacy URLs or syncing redirects from a CMS — can now read, bulk-update and delete redirect rules through the API or an AI assistant without touching the Sessionboard UI.

cs_action.note: Additive API change only; no UI surface changed. Customers must already have a custom domain configured on their Marketing pages (site_domains feature) before these endpoints return data rather than 404.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about managing Marketing page redirects at scale, automating domain migrations, or using the MCP server / AI assistants to maintain their event site's URL structure.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a custom domain on their Marketing pages who have developers or use AI assistants to manage their web presence programmatically.
internal.gotchas: The web-api backend (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5634) must be deployed first; until then these proxy rows return 404. The `if_version` parameter on PUT returns a 409 Conflict on a stale write — integrations should handle this.
internal.talk_track: If you manage redirects on your Marketing pages custom domain and want to automate that work — bulk imports, CMS sync, AI-assisted cleanup — these new API endpoints give you full read/write/delete access plus a full version history so you can always roll back.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and the /api/reference/overview guide should document the three new redirect-rules endpoints (GET with ?history, PUT with ops/restore_version/if_version, DELETE) under the Marketing pages section.
draft.why_use_it: The redirect rules API gives you full programmatic control over the URL redirects on your Marketing pages custom domain. Use it to migrate legacy paths in bulk, keep redirects in sync with an external CMS, or automate cleanup after a site restructure. The version history endpoint lets you audit every change — who made it, when, and exactly what moved — so you can roll back a bad batch with a single `restore_version` call.

entries.title: Set URL redirect rules on custom domains
entries.summary: Organizers can now define a list of redirect rules on each custom domain (e.g. `events.yourorg.com`). Each rule maps a **From** path to a **To** URL or path, with a **301** or **302** status and an **Enabled** toggle. Rules support exact paths, prefix wildcards (`/*`), and path carry-over; the edge answers them before any page loads. Every change creates a version with author and timestamp, and any version can be restored. Stale-write protection and loop/chain detection prevent conflicting rules.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Site Domains; then Marketing → Pages → Domains → [domain] → Redirects

entries.use_case: Organizers who have moved to a custom domain can redirect old paths (e.g. `/2024` → `/2025`) or send the whole domain root to a specific landing page without touching DNS or a separate tool. Useful when rebranding a site or retiring a URL that has been shared publicly.

cs_action.note: Site Domains is an on_request feature; the domain must already be connected before redirect rules appear.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about managing redirects on their custom domain, migrating from an old URL structure, or replicating Webflow-style redirect management inside Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have a custom domain connected and need to redirect legacy paths, run A/B landing-page tests, or forward the domain root to a specific event page.
internal.gotchas: Rules are answered at the edge with up to 60 seconds of cache; a newly added rule may take up to a minute to take effect. Loops and chains are blocked at write time — a rule whose target is itself redirected by another enabled rule will be rejected. Maximum 200 rules per domain.
internal.talk_track: Think of it like Webflow's redirect manager, but built into Sessionboard. You set a From path and a To destination, pick 301 or 302, and the edge handles it before any page loads. Every change is versioned so you can undo anything instantly.

draft.docs_gap: The /settings/domains guide should add a section explaining how to create, edit, enable/disable, and restore redirect rules on a custom domain, including prefix wildcard syntax and the version history/restore workflow.
draft.why_use_it: Redirect rules let you control what happens when someone visits a path on your custom domain that has moved or no longer exists. You can forward individual pages, entire path prefixes, or the domain root to any destination — with a permanent (301) or temporary (302) redirect — without leaving Sessionboard. A full version history means every change is auditable and any state can be restored in one click.

entries.title: Public API and MCP server expose a prioritised to-do list across all Marketing events
entries.summary: A new `GET /v1/marketing/outstanding` endpoint (MCP tool: `get_outstanding`) returns every outstanding Marketing task across an organisation's events — or for one event — as a structured to-do list. Each item includes a title, one-sentence explanation, urgency level (**now / soon / later**), a ready-to-run set of MCP tool calls, and a flag for whether a person must approve the action. AI assistants connected to Sessionboard can use this to surface and resolve outstanding items without the organiser having to hunt across events.
entries.use_case: Organisations running multiple webinars or events can ask their AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) "what needs my attention in Marketing?" and get a single prioritised list — content drafts awaiting approval, pages not yet live, recordings without a gate, missing hosts — with the exact steps to fix each one, rather than checking each event individually.

cs_action.note: The endpoint is available to any org with Marketing (beta). No configuration required; it is consumed by AI assistants via the MCP server or directly via the Public API.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with multiple webinars or events asks how to use their AI assistant to manage Marketing tasks, or when they ask about the MCP server's Marketing capabilities.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing beta customers who have connected an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to Sessionboard via MCP.
internal.staff_path: Public API: GET /v1/marketing/outstanding — no UI path; surfaced through AI assistant chat.
internal.gotchas: The listApprovals source requires a write-capable database connection; on read replicas it shows as 'unavailable' in the response. Coordinator drafts, speaker asks (Agent_Actions), Pathway review, host brief, and site tracking tags are listed as known gaps and will not appear as items yet.
internal.talk_track: If you connect your AI assistant to Sessionboard, you can ask 'what needs my attention in Marketing?' and get a single prioritised list across all your events — content to approve, pages to publish, recordings to gate — with the steps to fix each one.

draft.docs_gap: The guide at /sessionboard-marketing/outstanding should document the "Through the API" section with the endpoint path, the query parameters (event_id, product, limit), the shape of each item (id, kind, title, why, urgency, due, count, ask, do, needs_person_ok), and the top-level fields (lead, groups, counts, gaps, not_checked, unavailable).
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing tracks dozens of signals across your events — unpublished pages, ungated recordings, content awaiting approval, missing run-of-show details — but checking each event one by one takes time. The outstanding endpoint gives your AI assistant a single, prioritised view of everything that needs attention, complete with urgency ratings and ready-to-run fix instructions. Connect Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant to Sessionboard and ask what needs doing; the assistant reads the list, explains each item, and can act on the ones that do not need your explicit approval.

entries.title: Set an after-webinar plan that runs automatically when the webinar ends
entries.summary: A plan you configure before a webinar now runs by itself once the connected provider (Zoom, Goldcast, ON24, and others) marks it complete and the recording is in. The plan can import the recording, make content, gate the recording page, add it to a library gallery, send personalised attendee and no-show emails, deliver presenter share kits, and send a summary to the event owner and hosts. Emails and kits send only when the plan was **Approved** before the webinar started; otherwise they stay as drafts. Org-level defaults let you apply the same plan to every webinar automatically.

where.path: Marketing → Events → [webinar] → Follow-ups that run by themselves

entries.use_case: Teams running regular webinars can set the entire post-event workflow once — recording import, content creation, gating, library placement, speaker kits and audience emails — and have it execute without manual intervention the moment the webinar ends. Org-level defaults mean a new webinar inherits the plan automatically, so nothing falls through the cracks.

cs_action.note: Emails and presenter kits only send when the plan carries an approval fingerprint set before the webinar started. A self-serve org with no card on file gets drafts instead of live sends. Advise customers to approve the plan before the webinar goes live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs recurring webinars and wants to automate post-event follow-up — recording distribution, audience emails, speaker kits and content creation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any Marketing customer running webinars on Zoom, Goldcast, ON24, GoTo Webinar, Webex, Microsoft Teams or BigMarker who currently handles post-webinar steps manually.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → [webinar] → Follow-ups that run by themselves
internal.gotchas: The plan must be approved before the webinar starts for emails and kits to send live; editing the plan after approval resets the fingerprint and sends will revert to drafts. Self-serve orgs without a card on file always get drafts. The runner re-enqueues every 15 minutes until complete or until wait_hours have passed.
internal.talk_track: Instead of a checklist your team works through after every webinar, you set the plan once, approve it, and Sessionboard handles the recording, content, gating, speaker kits and audience emails the moment the webinar ends — attendees and no-shows each get a personalised email with the right link.

draft.docs_gap: The linked article /sessionboard-marketing/events/after-webinar-plan exists in the index and covers this feature; it should document the approval fingerprint mechanic, the org-level defaults path, the merge fields available in attendee/no-show emails, the gate options (off / before / at N seconds), and the results view (sent/opened/clicked, gate unlocks, viewers).
draft.why_use_it: After a webinar ends there are a dozen follow-up steps — importing the recording, making clips, gating the on-demand page, emailing attendees and no-shows, and getting speakers their share kits — that typically require someone to remember and execute each one. The after-webinar plan lets you define all of those steps before the webinar starts and have them run automatically the moment the provider confirms the webinar is over and the recording is ready. You approve the plan once; that approval is the signal that emails and kits are safe to send. Set org-level defaults so every new webinar inherits the same workflow without any extra setup.

entries.title: Agent pages support a gated video portal with chapters, time-codes and watch beacons
entries.summary: The **`<sb-portal kind="video">`** embed on agent pages now renders a full gated video player. A Capture form gates the video; once submitted, the player unlocks and focus moves to the video automatically. A return visitor who already unlocked skips the form. The player supports **chapters**, `#t=` time-code deep-links, a **Watch next** card, a CTA button, and privacy-respecting embeds for YouTube (nocookie) and Vimeo (dnt). Watch progress beacons (play, 25 %, 50 %, 75 %, 95 %, complete) are sent automatically.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the gated video portal; then the agent page will render the <sb-portal kind="video"> embed automatically

entries.use_case: Organizers who publish session recordings on agent pages can now gate those videos behind a Capture form, so they collect contact details before a visitor watches. Returning visitors who already unlocked the video skip the form entirely.

cs_action.note: Depends on the companion web-api PR (Agent pages: gated video portal, gallery recording routes and JSON-LD) being deployed first. Do not surface to customers until both PRs are live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about gating on-demand recordings on their agent or programme pages, or wants watch-engagement data from embedded videos.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using agent pages who want lead capture or watch analytics on their session recordings.
internal.gotchas: The watch grant is stored in localStorage on the agent page domain; sandboxed shared-host pages have no localStorage, so the skip-form behaviour will not work there. The PR was not browser-tested at merge time — it requires the web-api companion PR on dev before QA.
internal.talk_track: If you publish recordings on your agent pages, you can now gate them with a form. Visitors fill it in once and the video unlocks; come back later and it plays straight away. You also get chapter navigation, time-code links you can drop in emails, and automatic progress beacons so you know exactly how much of each recording people actually watch.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section documenting the <sb-portal kind="video"> embed on agent pages, including the Capture-form gate, the localStorage watch grant (and its absence on sandboxed hosts), chapter and #t= time-code syntax, the Watch next card, and the watch-progress beacon events.
draft.why_use_it: The gated video portal lets you put a lead-capture form in front of any recording published on an agent page. Visitors fill in the form once; after that, the player unlocks immediately on every return visit. Chapters, time-code links and a Watch next card keep viewers engaged, while automatic watch-progress beacons give you a precise picture of how far into each recording your audience gets.

entries.title: Marketing agent sites can host gated, SEO-ready webinar recording pages
entries.summary: Agent-built marketing sites now support a **`<sb-portal kind="video">`** component that renders a full recording player — including optional capture-form gating, chapters as seek buttons, captions, transcripts, and a "Watch next" list — directly on a page. A new **collection route** (`/webinars/{slug}`) generates one page per publicly visible gallery recording, complete with a sitemap entry. **JSON-LD** structured data (VideoObject, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage) is injected into the `<head>` of every live recording page so search engines and AI answer engines can index the content.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable agent site recording pages; then Marketing → Pages → Sites

entries.use_case: Organisations that run webinar libraries can publish a dedicated, branded page for every recording in a gallery — complete with a sign-up gate, transcript, chapters and "Watch next" links — without writing any custom code. Search engines and AI assistants index each page automatically via JSON-LD structured data, extending the reach of recorded content long after the live event.

cs_action.note: Requires the companion sessionboard-embeds (sb-portal.js) PR to be deployed before the player renders in a browser. The feature was unit-tested against real data but not yet click-tested in a running site; exercise on preview before enabling for a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to make their webinar recordings findable on Google or wants to gate on-demand content behind a lead-capture form on their own branded site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with an active webinar programme and a content gallery who want SEO-indexed, gated recording pages without a custom CMS.
internal.gotchas: Gallery item thumbnails may be presigned S3 URLs (24-hour expiry); a stable poster via request_page_upload is recommended for the VideoObject thumbnailUrl. Clip pages show no transcript of their own — captions borrow the parent recording's lines. Up to 4 video portals per page. The embeds PR must be deployed to dev before browser testing.
internal.talk_track: Every recording in your gallery can now have its own SEO page with a lead-capture gate, chapters, transcript and a 'Watch next' rail — all built automatically from the data you already have in Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the `<sb-portal kind="video">` component attributes, the collection route configuration (`/webinars/{slug}` with `bind { collection: "gallery:<id>" }`), how to set up the capture-form gate (placement `recording_gate`), the JSON-LD types that are emitted, and the 4-portal-per-page cap.
draft.why_use_it: Recording pages let you turn every webinar in your gallery into a standalone, discoverable web page that search engines and AI answer engines can read and rank. Each page carries the player, a capture-form gate to collect leads, a full transcript, chapter seek buttons, and automatic "Watch next" suggestions — all generated from the data already in your gallery. Use recording pages when you want on-demand content to drive registrations and grow your audience beyond the people who attended live.

entries.title: Public API: manage on-demand library items and update recording metadata
entries.summary: Two new API route groups are available under `write:marketing` and `read:marketing` scopes. `GET /v1/marketing/pages/galleries/:galleryId/items` and `PUT …/items` let integrations read and write the exact recordings in an on-demand library — add, remove, reorder, feature items by media or content ID, and override the gallery's automatic rules with `onlyChosen`. `PUT /v1/marketing/content/recordings/:mediaId` lets integrations set or update a recording's event association, title, description, and tags after import.
entries.use_case: Teams that manage on-demand libraries programmatically — for example, syncing a post-event video catalogue from an external system — can now control exactly which recordings appear in a library and keep recording metadata (title, description, tags, event) accurate without logging into Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Routes are additive API endpoints; no UI change. Customers must already have the content_galleries feature and use API tokens with read:marketing / write:marketing scopes.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about automating their on-demand library curation or keeping recording metadata in sync from an external video or event platform.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Content Galleries enabled who use the public API to manage their marketing content programmatically.
internal.gotchas: The companion web-api PR (#5631) must be deployed first; until it is live these routes return 404. The onlyChosen flag disables the gallery's automatic inclusion rules — advise customers to test before using in production.
internal.talk_track: If you manage recordings or on-demand libraries from an external system, the API now lets you control exactly what's in each library and keep recording titles, descriptions and tags up to date without touching the Sessionboard UI.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new API endpoints for reading and writing library items (including the onlyChosen parameter) and for updating recording metadata, with example request/response shapes and scope requirements.
draft.why_use_it: The on-demand library lets you publish a curated collection of recordings on a branded page. Managing library contents and recording metadata through the API means your video catalogue stays in sync with external systems automatically, without manual updates in the Sessionboard UI.

entries.title: Hand-pick exactly which recordings appear in an on-demand library, and move a recording to a different event after import
entries.summary: Two new controls for on-demand libraries: **Only chosen** mode lets you select individual recordings for a library instead of pulling in everything that matches a rule, and a recording's event can now be set, moved, or cleared after it has been imported — so YouTube imports with no event can be assigned to the right one without re-importing. Org-wide libraries automatically exclude Zoom meeting recordings (calls), keeping webinar content separate from internal call recordings.
entries.use_case: An org that runs both public webinars and internal customer calls can now build a library that holds exactly the 24 webinar recordings it wants — mixing recordings from different events and YouTube imports — without exposing call recordings or unrelated content. After importing a YouTube video with no event attached, the organizer can assign it to the correct event without re-importing.

cs_action.note: Both controls are available to any org using Content Galleries (preview). No configuration required beyond the customer using the new Items panel.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has a mix of webinar and internal call recordings in Media and wants a public library with only specific recordings, or when they have imported YouTube videos that landed without an event association.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who run on-demand libraries and whose org Media holds recordings from multiple events or sources — especially those mixing Zoom webinars with Zoom meeting recordings.
internal.gotchas: Only chosen mode is refused if the library uses registrant-only access or an event-bound template. Removing a rule-matched item while a rule is still active hides it (so a sync cannot re-add it) rather than deleting it. Moving a recording's event clears any session link on the old event and requires the caller to have access to both events.
internal.talk_track: If your Media library holds both webinar recordings and internal call recordings, you can now build a library that shows exactly the recordings you choose — no rules pulling in content you don't want. And if you imported a YouTube video before you knew which event it belonged to, you can assign it to the right event now without starting over.

draft.docs_gap: The guide at /sessionboard-marketing/pages/choose-library-items should document how to enable Only chosen mode, how to add and remove individual recordings by id, how ordering works (switches the library sort to curated), how the org-wide call exclusion rule works and how to override it with include_calls, and how to set or move a recording's event from the recording detail view.
draft.why_use_it: On-demand libraries let you publish a curated collection of recordings on a branded page your audience can browse and watch. Choosing items by hand gives you precise control over what appears — useful when your Media library holds recordings from multiple sources or purposes and you want only a specific set in front of your audience. Org-wide libraries automatically keep Zoom meeting recordings (calls) out of rule-based results, so webinar content stays separate from internal recordings unless you explicitly add them.

entries.title: Agent pages and content galleries automatically send GA4/GTM conversion events and attribution
entries.summary: Agent pages and content galleries now push conversion events to GA4 and GTM without any custom script. Events include **sb_form_submit** (capture and registration forms), **sb_cta_click** (button and link clicks), **sb_video_gate_unlocked**, **sb_video_play**, and **sb_video_progress** (at 25 %, 50 %, 75 % and 100 %). Each sign-up, gate unlock and registration checkout also carries UTM, click-ID and first-touch attribution fields. No personal data (email, name, company) is ever sent to the dataLayer.

where.path: Marketing → Pages → Content Gallery / Agent pages

entries.use_case: Marketers who run GA4 or GTM on their site can now see exactly which form submissions, video plays, gate unlocks and CTA clicks came from agent pages and content galleries — and trace each conversion back to its UTM source — without writing a single line of custom tracking code.

cs_action.note: The API half (sessionboard-web-api#5632) must be deployed to production before this bundle is published to prod. Merging this PR deploys to DEV only. Confirm prod release order before announcing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to track form conversions or video engagement from their agent pages or content galleries in GA4 or GTM.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using agent pages or content galleries who has GA4 or GTM on their site and wants conversion data without custom scripting.
internal.gotchas: The web-api PR #5632 must ship to prod first — the API rejects new attribution keys until then. Also: on Sessionboard-hosted pages, cookies and localStorage are sandboxed, so attribution falls back to the current page view.
internal.talk_track: Your agent pages and content galleries now automatically fire GA4/GTM events for every form submit, video play and CTA click — with UTM and click-ID attribution — so you can see exactly what's driving conversions without any custom code.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the full list of dataLayer event names and their parameters (sb_form_submit, sb_cta_click, sb_video_gate_unlocked, sb_video_play, sb_video_progress), explain that attribution fields are appended automatically, and note that no PII is included in any event.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard pages and content galleries push structured conversion events directly into your GA4 property or GTM dataLayer, so every form submission, video play, gate unlock and CTA click appears in your existing analytics dashboards. Attribution fields — UTM parameters, click IDs and first-touch landing page — travel with each event, letting you credit the right campaign for every sign-up or registration. No personal data is included, and events are deduplicated so nothing is counted twice when both gtag.js and GTM are present.

entries.title: Set Site analytics IDs via the Public API and AI assistants
entries.summary: The Public API and MCP server now expose `GET/PUT /v1/sites/tracking` (org default) and `GET/PUT /v1/sites/:siteId/tracking` (per-site override), letting integrations read and write **GTM Container ID**, **GA4 Measurement ID**, **HubSpot Portal ID**, **HubSpot Region**, **LinkedIn Partner ID**, and **Meta Pixel ID** for any Site. Passing `null` for a field clears it. Requires the `read:sites` or `write:sites` API scope.
entries.use_case: Teams that manage multiple Sites programmatically — or through an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT — can now push analytics IDs in bulk without opening each Site in the UI, making it easy to roll out a new GTM container or swap a GA4 property across every event site at once.

cs_action.note: Endpoints are available to any customer with a Public API token that carries read:sites or write:sites scope. No feature flag required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about automating Site setup, managing analytics IDs across many events, or using the MCP server to configure Sites.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with multiple Sites who want to manage analytics tags programmatically or via an AI assistant.
internal.gotchas: The org-level endpoint sets the default every Site inherits; the per-site endpoint overrides it for one Site. Passing null clears a field rather than leaving it unchanged.
internal.talk_track: If you manage analytics IDs across many event Sites, you can now read and update GTM, GA4, HubSpot, LinkedIn and Meta IDs through the API or by asking your AI assistant — no need to open each Site individually.

draft.docs_gap: The Site builder guide should document the new /v1/sites/tracking and /v1/sites/:siteId/tracking API endpoints, including the available fields (GTM, GA4, HubSpot, LinkedIn, Meta), how null clears a value, and the required read:sites / write:sites scopes.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Sites support several analytics and advertising tags — Google Tag Manager, GA4, HubSpot, LinkedIn and Meta — so you can measure visitor behaviour and attribute registrations without writing custom code. The tracking API lets you read and update those IDs programmatically, which is useful when you manage many Sites or want an AI assistant to configure analytics as part of a broader site-setup workflow.

entries.title: Recording pages get AI-generated summaries, key takeaways, FAQ, SEO fields, and transcript-from-text upload
entries.summary: When a recording's transcript is ready, Sessionboard automatically writes an **AI Summary** (2–3 sentence overview, 4–6 **Key Takeaways**, and structured **Sections**) for the recording page — replacing the raw transcript opening that previously appeared under "What this webinar covers." Organizers can also set or override **Summary**, **Key Takeaways**, **Sections**, **FAQ**, **SEO Title** (≤60 chars) and **Meta Description** (≤160 chars) per recording; a person's value always wins over the AI's, field by field. A new **Add Transcript** endpoint lets organizers attach transcript lines to recordings whose download failed (for example, YouTube imports blocked by the provider), triggering speaker resolution, chapters, and the summary automatically. Recording pages also gain **FAQPage** and **VideoObject** JSON-LD structured data, and library pages gain **CollectionPage + ItemList** markup for search engines.
entries.use_case: Organizers who publish on-demand webinar recording pages no longer need to write summaries by hand — the AI drafts a structured overview, takeaways, and sections the moment a transcript is ready, so every recording page is immediately useful to visitors. Teams with YouTube recordings that failed to download can now paste in transcript text directly to unlock chapters, clips, and the summary without re-importing the video.

cs_action.note: AI summary is default-on for all customers with transcripts. The flag MEDIA_AUTO_SUMMARY can be disabled per workspace if a customer objects to automatic AI writes. A backfill task (backfill-recording-summaries) must be run post-release to generate summaries for existing recordings that already have transcripts but no summary — coordinate with engineering.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their recording pages show raw transcript text instead of a proper description, or when they want better SEO on their on-demand library.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer publishing webinar recording pages, especially those with large back-catalogues of recordings or YouTube imports that failed to download.
internal.gotchas: Summaries only generate after a transcript is in 'ready' status. YouTube recordings blocked by yt-dlp (402 proxy errors) will not have transcripts unless the organizer uploads transcript lines via the new Add Transcript endpoint or the public API. The backfill task defaults to 200 recordings per run and must be re-run if 'more: true' is returned. A person's field value always wins over the AI's — clearing a field (setting it to null) restores the AI value.
internal.talk_track: Every recording page now writes itself — the AI reads the transcript and produces a summary, takeaways, and FAQ that visitors and search engines can use. You can override any field, and your words always win. For recordings that never got a transcript because YouTube blocked the download, you can now paste in the transcript text and everything — chapters, clips, summary — follows automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new page fields (Summary, Key Takeaways, Sections, FAQ, SEO Title, Meta Description), how AI-generated values are overridden by organizer-entered values, the regenerateSummary option, the Add Transcript from text endpoint for failed downloads, and the new JSON-LD structured data types (FAQPage, CollectionPage, ItemList) emitted by recording and library pages.
draft.why_use_it: Recording pages give every webinar a permanent, searchable home where visitors can read what a session covers, skim key takeaways, and find answers to common questions before deciding to watch. Structured SEO fields and JSON-LD markup help search engines and AI assistants surface the right recording to the right audience. When you set a custom summary or FAQ, your words take precedence over the AI draft — so the page always reflects your voice and your event's brand.

entries.title: Attach a transcript to a recording via the API or AI assistant
entries.summary: A new `POST /v1/marketing/content/recordings/:mediaId/transcript` endpoint lets integrations and AI assistants (via the `add_recording_transcript` MCP tool) attach a pre-existing transcript — speaker labels, start times and text lines — to a recording whose automatic download failed. The endpoint requires a write scope on Marketing content, consistent with other content write operations.
entries.use_case: When a recording's automatic transcript download fails — for example because the source platform's export timed out — an organizer or their integration can push the transcript they already have directly to the recording, so clips, recaps and search all have accurate text without re-processing the video.

cs_action.note: API-only change; no UI surface changes. Customers using the public API or an AI assistant connected via MCP can call the new endpoint immediately.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that a recording's transcript is missing or blank after import, especially when the source platform's download failed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who manage post-production transcripts outside Sessionboard or who use the MCP server / AI assistants to automate content workflows.
internal.gotchas: The endpoint is proxied through the Marketing public-API layer; web-api enforces scope and ownership checks. The companion page-copy fields (summary, keyTakeaways, faq, seoTitle, metaDescription, regenerateSummary) on update_recording ride the existing PUT route and are not part of this change.
internal.talk_track: If a recording came in without a transcript — maybe the download timed out — you can now push the transcript you already have straight to that recording via the API or your AI assistant, and all the downstream content tools will pick it up.

draft.docs_gap: The Playbook 1 section should document the new POST /v1/marketing/content/recordings/:mediaId/transcript endpoint, its required body shape (speaker, start, text lines), required scopes, and the add_recording_transcript MCP tool name.
draft.why_use_it: The Media & Transcriptions API lets you keep recordings and their transcripts in sync between Sessionboard and your other systems. You can upload transcript text with speaker labels and timestamps, attach it to any recording, and immediately unlock downstream features — clips, recaps, quotes and AI-generated content — that depend on accurate transcription. Use it when your webinar platform, AV team or post-production workflow produces transcripts outside Sessionboard's automatic pipeline.

entries.title: One email gate per page view unlocks both gated takeaways and gated videos
entries.summary: Visitors to a gated recording page now complete the email gate only once per page view. After submitting the gate form, the grant is held in page memory (not stored in the browser), so a page reload shows the gate again. Clicking a gated takeaway link opens the **#sb-asset-gate** modal with focus on the email field; after submitting, the dialog offers the requested file as a direct link. A grant earned from a video gate also unlocks takeaway links on the same page, and vice versa — a takeaway gate grant opens the video through the watch URL. Files that are already open (ungated) skip the modal entirely.
entries.use_case: Organizers who gate webinar recordings and share downloadable takeaways (slides, handouts) on the same page can now offer a single, friction-free gate: a visitor fills in their email once and immediately accesses both the video and any gated files without being prompted again during that visit.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic for all gated recording pages. The grant is no longer written to localStorage, so the previous 'Welcome back' restore for video gates is gone — visitors who return in a new tab or after a reload will see the gate again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about gating webinar recordings alongside downloadable content, or when they report that visitors were being asked to fill in the email gate multiple times on the same page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using gated recording pages with takeaway file links.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Pages → Recording page → gate settings
internal.gotchas: The localStorage grant for video gates has been removed. Visitors who previously saw a 'Welcome back' message on return visits will now see the gate again. This is intentional — each page load is a fresh lead capture. Also note that PROD publish of embeds is manual; confirm the deploy has run before telling customers the change is live.
internal.talk_track: Visitors now fill in their email once per page visit and that single grant unlocks both the video and any gated takeaway files on the page — no repeated prompts. Because the grant isn't saved to the browser, every new visit is a fresh capture opportunity.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the email gate modal for takeaway files (the #sb-asset-gate modal), explain the single-grant-per-page-view behaviour, and note that the grant is not persisted across page loads.
draft.why_use_it: Gated recording pages let you capture leads from on-demand webinar content without requiring a full registration form. Visitors submit their email to unlock the recording, and the same gate can protect downloadable takeaways such as slides or handouts on the same page. Because the grant lives only in page memory, every new visit is a fresh lead capture opportunity, while the single-gate-per-visit experience keeps friction low for genuine viewers.

entries.title: Advocacy campaign detail page gains a Setup tab and a smarter Analytics empty state
entries.summary: A new **Setup** tab on each Advocacy campaign consolidates **Reminders**, **Rewards** and **Conversion tracking** into one place, removing those cards from the top of the page so results are visible without scrolling. When a campaign has no shares, clicks or landing views yet, the **Analytics** tab shows a single contextual card instead of four zero-value tiles: if no recipients have been added it says "No one is sharing yet" and offers an **Add recipients** button that opens the **Recipients** tab; if recipients are already assigned it shows how many people are sharing.
entries.use_case: Organizers setting up a new campaign no longer have to scroll past empty KPI tiles and setup cards to reach their results. The Setup tab keeps configuration out of the way once a campaign is live, and the Analytics empty state guides them to add recipients before expecting data.

cs_action.note: Layout change is automatic for all Advocacy campaigns. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says the campaign page feels cluttered or they can't find where to set up reminders or rewards.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using Advocacy campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → open any campaign → Setup tab or Analytics tab
internal.gotchas: The Setup tab is hidden in demo mode, matching the previous behaviour of the individual setup cards. Link-or-embed campaigns keep their existing notice in Analytics and are not affected by the new empty state.
internal.talk_track: The campaign page is cleaner now — Reminders, Rewards and Conversion tracking all live under a Setup tab, so the Analytics view shows your results right away. And if a campaign hasn't had any activity yet, Analytics tells you exactly what to do next instead of showing a wall of zeros.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Setup tab (path, what it contains) and describe the Analytics empty-state card and its "Add recipients" shortcut.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets you turn speakers, sponsors, exhibitors and attendees into active promoters of your event by giving each person a personalised share card and tracking every click and conversion that results. Use it when you want to extend your event's reach through the networks of the people already involved, without running separate social ad campaigns. The campaign detail page shows you who is sharing, what is working and where conversions are coming from, so you can follow up with the right people at the right time.

entries.title: Control how search engines and AI crawlers index your Marketing pages
entries.summary: A new **Search engines & AI** card on Marketing → Pages lets organizers control indexing, AI crawler access, llms.txt publishing and canonical addresses per site. Every Marketing Site gets a **Let search engines index this site** toggle; agent sites also get **Let AI assistants and AI training crawlers read it**, **Publish llms.txt**, and an optional **Canonical address** field for reverse-proxied domains. Individual pages on agent sites can be hidden from search engines with a per-page **Hide this page from search engines** toggle. Direct links to each site's `sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt` are included. When an org has more than one Marketing Site, a site picker appears at the top of the card.
entries.use_case: Organizers who host Marketing Sites under their own domain, or who want to control whether AI training crawlers can read their content, can now manage all SEO and discoverability settings in one place without touching DNS or server config. Teams running multiple sites can switch between them with the site picker and configure each independently.

cs_action.note: All settings default to on; no action required unless a customer wants to restrict crawlers or set a canonical address.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about SEO for their Marketing Site, wants to block AI crawlers, or is reverse-proxying their site under a custom domain and needs to set a canonical URL.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Marketing Sites who cares about search visibility, AI discoverability, or has their site served under their own domain.
internal.gotchas: The Canonical address, AI crawler toggle, llms.txt toggle, and per-page hide controls are only available on agent sites (not plain event pages). Per-page hide changes save to the draft and go live at publish — remind customers to publish after toggling.
internal.talk_track: You now have a single card to control everything about how search engines and AI tools see your Marketing Site — indexing, AI crawlers, llms.txt, canonical address, and even hiding individual pages. It all defaults to on, so there's nothing to set up unless you want to restrict something.

draft.docs_gap: The article at /sessionboard-marketing/pages/search-engines-and-ai exists in the index and appears to cover this feature; confirm it documents the site picker behaviour for multi-site orgs and the distinction between agent sites and event pages.
draft.why_use_it: The Search engines & AI card gives you direct control over how your Marketing Sites appear — or don't appear — in search results and AI-generated answers. Toggle indexing on or off per site, decide whether AI assistants and training crawlers can read your content, publish an llms.txt hint file, and set a canonical address when your site is served under your own domain. Per-page overrides let you keep specific pages out of search results while the rest of the site remains fully indexed.

entries.title: Agent sites are now crawlable by search engines and AI by default, with per-site controls
entries.summary: Agent sites (e.g. `/p/{slug}`) are indexed by search engines and AI crawlers by default — no extra step required. A new **Search engines & AI** setting on each site lets organizers turn indexing off, block AI crawlers separately, set a canonical base URL, and enable or disable `llms.txt`. Pages can also be excluded individually. The sitemap and `llms.txt` file update automatically to reflect these settings.
entries.use_case: Organizers who publish agent sites for content like webinars or on-demand libraries can now have those sites discovered and indexed by Google and AI assistants automatically, without any configuration. Teams that need to keep a site private or control AI crawling can turn those options off per site.

cs_action.note: Indexing is on by default for all agent sites. Customers who previously expected their /p/{slug} sites to be unindexed should be told to turn off the Search engines & AI setting. No action needed for customers who want discoverability.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how their agent site content gets found in Google or AI tools, or when they want to keep a site private from search engines.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using agent sites for public-facing content such as webinar libraries, on-demand hubs or program pages.
internal.gotchas: The seo column is nullable; null means all settings are on. Existing sites with no seo value are treated as fully indexable from the moment this ships. Customers who want noindex must explicitly turn it off.
internal.talk_track: Agent sites are now crawlable out of the box — Google and AI assistants like ChatGPT can find and surface your content. If you need a site to stay private, there's a per-site toggle to turn indexing off, and you can block AI crawlers separately from regular search engines.

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should document the new per-site Search engines & AI panel: the index toggle, the AI crawlers toggle, the canonical base URL field, the llms.txt toggle, how to exclude individual pages, and how the sitemap and llms.txt endpoints reflect these settings.
draft.why_use_it: Search engines and AI assistants read your agent sites to surface your content in search results and AI-generated answers. Controlling indexing per site lets you make public content discoverable while keeping preview or private sites out of search. The sitemap and llms.txt file are generated automatically so crawlers always have an accurate picture of what is available.
